Top 5 recorded entries:

# Value-ref false-positive handling

Lifecycle status: accepted

During value-reference validation, false-positive clusters must be fixed while isolated singletons are recorded as known residuals. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §0 instructs agents to hunt FPs during the validation sweep, fix FP clusters, and record singletons.

# Measure before assuming holes

Lifecycle status: accepted

Measure framework usage before assuming a dynamic-dispatch hole; Svelte's presumed event-handler gap was not the real gap because modern Svelte often uses form actions and callback props instead of `on:click={fn}`. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 explicitly states this lesson in the Svelte/SvelteKit row.

# Declared return types define chain fit

Lifecycle status: accepted

The lesson from #750 is that chained-call support fits languages with reliably declared return types, not the broader or narrower label of statically typed languages. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 says the original statically-typed README enumeration was incomplete and the through-line is reliable declared return types.

# Constant read node check

Lifecycle status: accepted

A new value-reference language must confirm the grammar node type used for constant reads before sweeping, because a reader-scan mismatch produces zero edges even when targets register correctly. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A names this as the PHP lesson: PHP constant references are `name` nodes, not `identifier` or `constant`, so edges did not form until `name` was added to `flushValueRefs`.

# Parent-kind sample check

Lifecycle status: accepted

Before enabling value references for the next class-scope language, inspect the parent kind of a sample constant and widen the target gate when that shared parent kind is missing. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A explicitly calls this the lesson for the next class-scope language and says missing `struct:`, `enum:`, or `interface:`-style parent kinds make the feature silently emit nothing despite nodes existing.

Top 5 recorded entries:

# Universal dynamic-dispatch coverage

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should close dynamic-dispatch static-extraction coverage holes across every supported language and framework so cross-symbol flows exist in the graph everywhere. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Mission says to systematically close dynamic dispatch holes across every language and framework CodeGraph supports and validate each one the same way.

# Dynamic boundary detector

Lifecycle status: accepted

`src/mcp/dynamic-boundaries.ts` is the CodeGraph component that surfaces dynamic dispatch boundaries when a static trace cannot safely synthesize an edge. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 3 names `src/mcp/dynamic-boundaries.ts` and #687 as the boundary-surfacing mechanism.

# ORM metaprogramming frontier

Lifecycle status: superseded

CodeGraph has not yet resolved ORM metaprogramming dispatch for EF Core LINQ/DbSet, ActiveRecord dynamic finders, or Eloquent dynamic finders and relationships. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks these as hole-identified frontiers in the ASP.NET Core, Rails, and Laravel rows.

# No explosion dispatch validation

Top 5 recorded entries:

# Function-ref registration capture

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ships function-as-value registration capture by extracting deterministic value-position candidates, gating them, resolving them as internal `function_ref` references, and emitting ordinary `references` edges with function-ref metadata. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Mechanism describes the capture → gate → unresolved `function_ref` → exact resolution → `references` edge pipeline and says callers/callees/impact radius already traverse `references`, so no graph-layer changes were needed.

# Function reference capture pipeline

Lifecycle status: accepted

The function reference capture pipeline is the CodeGraph extraction and resolution path for function-as-value registration sites. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Mechanism names `src/extraction/function-ref.ts`, `flushFnRefCandidates`, internal `referenceKind: 'function_ref'`, `resolveOne`, `resolveViaImport`, `matchFunctionRef`, and `src/resolution/index.ts`.

# Function-ref validation invariants

Lifecycle status: accepted

Function-ref capture must prove node counts identical, `calls` edges unchanged, `references` strictly additive, sampled `fnRef` edges precise, and unresolved ref batches drained. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Validation says the 2026-06-11 A/B used fresh public OSS clones, identical nodes, untouched calls, additive references, source-line spot checks, and fully drained `unresolved_refs`.

# Additive function-ref references

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shipped function-ref capture adds registration-site `references` edges while leaving nodes and `calls` edges unchanged across the validation corpus. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Validation reports all 17 repos had identical nodes and 0/0 calls deltas, with strictly additive refs such as redis +1918, Pascal +577, Swift +116, and TS/React +121.

# Function-ref shadowing residual

Lifecycle status: accepted

Function-ref capture accepts a residual ambiguity where local variables or parameters shadow imported or same-file functions, because resolving it would require local-scope tracking beyond the deliberately uncovered data-flow frontier. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits reports roughly 1-2 such cases per 20 sampled edges on callback-heavy repos while the file-level dependency was real in every observed case.

Top 5 recorded entries:

# Measure before assuming holes

Lifecycle status: accepted

Measure framework usage before assuming a dynamic-dispatch hole; Svelte's presumed event-handler gap was not the real gap because modern Svelte often uses form actions and callback props instead of `on:click={fn}`. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 explicitly states this lesson in the Svelte/SvelteKit row.

# Universal dynamic-dispatch coverage

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should close dynamic-dispatch static-extraction coverage holes across every supported language and framework so cross-symbol flows exist in the graph everywhere. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Mission says to systematically close dynamic dispatch holes across every language and framework CodeGraph supports and validate each one the same way.

# Trace wrongness masquerades as adoption floor

Lifecycle status: accepted

A small repo read-heavy result can be a fixable trace endpoint bug rather than an adoption floor; compare what the agent read with the tool output immediately before it. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3d says Alamofire was misread as the small-repo floor until transcripts showed the tool returned wrong stub endpoints, and the methodology lesson says transcript reasoning, not the median, tells which case it is.

# Dynamic boundary detector

Lifecycle status: accepted

`src/mcp/dynamic-boundaries.ts` is the CodeGraph component that surfaces dynamic dispatch boundaries when a static trace cannot safely synthesize an edge. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 3 names `src/mcp/dynamic-boundaries.ts` and #687 as the boundary-surfacing mechanism.

# No explosion dispatch validation

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dynamic-dispatch coverage changes must keep node count stable, avoid regressions on a control repo, and spot-check synthesized or resolved edges for precise targets before being considered successful. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 5 and Success criteria require no node explosion, no control-repo regression, and precise spot-checked synthesized edges.

content.text:
Top 5 recorded entries:

# Value-ref false-positive handling

Lifecycle status: accepted

During value-reference validation, false-positive clusters must be fixed while isolated singletons are recorded as known residuals. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §0 instructs agents to hunt FPs during the validation sweep, fix FP clusters, and record singletons.

# Pascal case-sensitive misses

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value-reference scanning may miss references that differ only by case because Pascal is case-insensitive while the reader scan matches exact text; this is a false negative, not a false positive. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says differently-cased Pascal references are missed and not worth normalizing.

# Sibling class constant ambiguity

Lifecycle status: accepted

The file-wide class-scope target map accepts a residual false-positive risk when sibling classes in the same file define the same constant name. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A says this is the only real false-positive case, observed at about 1.7% of Ruby targets on Rails, and valid code rarely hits it because a bare sibling-class constant is a Ruby NameError.

# Pascal const-param parse residual

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value refs accept a small residual false-positive tail where tree-sitter-pascal can context-dependently misparse a complex Delphi `const` parameter as `declConst`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 says this parse-fidelity FP remains after restricting Pascal targets to `constant` only and is documented as an accepted caveat.

# CommonJS bindings are value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

CommonJS `var x = require(...)` bindings and module-level mutable state should not be treated as value-ref false positives when same-file readers actually depend on them. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §3 says these are correct same-file reads, changing the binding affects readers, impact deduplicates against `calls` edges, and higher JS edge share is fine if precision holds.

Top 5 recorded entries:

# Value-ref parent-kind gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference targets must register only under shared-scope parents accepted by the target gate: file, class, module, struct, or enum. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A says the target gate now accepts `file:`, `class:`, `module:`, `struct:`, and `enum:` parents, and warns that a missing parent kind makes a language silently emit no value-reference edges even when constant nodes exist.

# Parent-kind sample check

Lifecycle status: accepted

Before enabling value references for the next class-scope language, inspect the parent kind of a sample constant and widen the target gate when that shared parent kind is missing. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A explicitly calls this the lesson for the next class-scope language and says missing `struct:`, `enum:`, or `interface:`-style parent kinds make the feature silently emit nothing despite nodes existing.

# Value-ref extractor kind check

Lifecycle status: accepted

A value-reference language extension must confirm that sample module-level constants are emitted as `constant` or `variable` before relying on the target gate. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5C says `captureValueRefScope` keys targets off `kind in {constant, variable}` and instructs agents to query indexed sample nodes, adjusting the target gate if constants instead emit as `field`, `property`, `import`, or another kind.

# Exact valueRef edge filter

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-ref validation queries must filter exact value-reference edges with `kind='references'` and metadata containing `"valueRef":true`, not broad `LIKE '%valueRef%'` matching. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §4.1 says the precise filter is required because broad LIKE matches filenames such as `textModelValueReference.ts`.

# JVM and CSharp const-field kind switch

Lifecycle status: accepted

Java and C# value-reference support emits only shared const-like fields as `constant` while leaving instance `final` and `readonly` fields as `field`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says Java `static final` and C# `const`/`static readonly` use an `isConst` predicate plus `extractField` kind switch, while instance final/readonly fields stay `field`.

# Pascal case-sensitive misses

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value-reference scanning may miss references that differ only by case because Pascal is case-insensitive while the reader scan matches exact text; this is a false negative, not a false positive. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says differently-cased Pascal references are missed and not worth normalizing.

# Pascal const value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value-reference support adds Pascal to the enabled language set, uses existing unit/class `const` extraction, adds `declConst`/`declVar` shadow pruning, and extends reader scanning to the sibling `block` body of procedure headers. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says Pascal was add-to-`VALUE_REF_LANGS` plus shadow prune and the same sibling-body fix as Dart for `block` siblings under `defProc`.

# Pascal const-param parse residual

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value refs accept a small residual false-positive tail where tree-sitter-pascal can context-dependently misparse a complex Delphi `const` parameter as `declConst`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 says this parse-fidelity FP remains after restricting Pascal targets to `constant` only and is documented as an accepted caveat.

# Same-file value-ref yield limit

Lifecycle status: accepted

Same-file-only value-reference capture has lower yield in languages where constants are commonly read cross-file or cross-unit, such as PHP and Pascal, but remains correct rather than noisy. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says PHP and Pascal have low yield because reads are often cross-file/cross-unit while value-refs remain same-file only.

# Pascal constant-only value-ref targets

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value-ref target capture must restrict targets to `constant` nodes only, because its extractor emits parameters and class fields as `variable` at a broad parent scope that would collapse into noisy file-wide targets. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 says the genuine shared values were all `constant` (`declConst`) and the fix is a per-language restriction in `captureValueRefScope`.

# Function-ref registration capture

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ships function-as-value registration capture by extracting deterministic value-position candidates, gating them, resolving them as internal `function_ref` references, and emitting ordinary `references` edges with function-ref metadata. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Mechanism describes the capture → gate → unresolved `function_ref` → exact resolution → `references` edge pipeline and says callers/callees/impact radius already traverse `references`, so no graph-layer changes were needed.

# Constant read node check

Lifecycle status: accepted

A new value-reference language must confirm the grammar node type used for constant reads before sweeping, because a reader-scan mismatch produces zero edges even when targets register correctly. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A names this as the PHP lesson: PHP constant references are `name` nodes, not `identifier` or `constant`, so edges did not form until `name` was added to `flushValueRefs`.

Lifecycle status: accepted

Function-ref resolution must match only function or method targets in the same language family, prefer same-file exact matches, allow cross-file matches only when unique, avoid self-loops, and never use fuzzy fallback. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Mechanism and Precision rule 9 state `resolveViaImport` then `matchFunctionRef`, exact names only, same-file first, unique cross-file only, ambiguity yields no edge, and `matchReference` short-circuits `function_ref` refs to avoid fuzzy fallback.

# Declared return types define chain fit

Lifecycle status: accepted

The lesson from #750 is that chained-call support fits languages with reliably declared return types, not the broader or narrower label of statically typed languages. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 says the original statically-typed README enumeration was incomplete and the through-line is reliable declared return types.

# Chained call resolver

Lifecycle status: accepted

The chained call resolver is the CodeGraph resolution/extraction surface for factory and fluent calls whose receiver is itself a call. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 names `src/resolution/name-matcher.ts`, `resolution/index.ts`, `tree-sitter.ts`, bespoke extractors, and `languages/*.ts` as the components for chained static-factory and fluent call resolution.

# Conformance chained-call pass

Lifecycle status: accepted

Failed chained-call refs in `CHAIN_LANGUAGES` are deferred and re-resolved after inheritance and conformance edges exist, walking supertypes for inherited, default-interface, trait, mixin, and embedded methods. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Conformance pass (#754) describes `resolveChainedCallsViaConformance()` after edges exist.

# Shared chained-call resolvers

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph centralizes chained-call matching in three shared resolvers in `src/resolution/name-matcher.ts`: C/C++ field-expression chains, PHP/Rust scoped chains, and dotted chains for Java-family and similar languages. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 lists `matchCppCallChain`, `matchScopedCallChain`, and `matchDottedCallChain`, all calling `resolveMethodOnType`.

# Declared-return chained-call mechanism

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped a three-part mechanism for chained static-factory and fluent call resolution across 13 languages: capture declared return types, preserve chained receivers at extraction, then resolve and validate the outer method on the returned type. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Status and The 3-part mechanism describe the shipped design for C++, C, PHP, Java, Kotlin, C#, Swift, Rust, Go, Scala, Dart, Objective-C, and Pascal/Delphi.
